solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: One headless attack in case of mate at end of tether?

definitions.text: One headless attack in case of mate at end of tether?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the attack goes within the outer pair
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of mate are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of mate

indicators.note: without a head means the word for attack loses its opening letter

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a pound'
an onslaught is a fierce attack; it loses its first letter

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of tether is used

parts.note: the final letter of tether

explanation.surface: A spouse at the end of their tether lashes out, with one assault leaving a partner dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Anslaught is an old form of onslaught. Read whole, the clue also describes the crime itself: killing a mate in a moment of desperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is unlawful killing without premeditation, the likely charge for someone who kills a spouse when driven beyond endurance.

clue.text: A hateful guy, do not spare him

indicators.note: to do something over is to work it into a new form, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: all eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to show no mercy to a loathsome man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do not' reads as a single instruction, but 'do' alone signals the rearrangement and 'not spare him' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope hates humankind, so he is a person full of hatred towards others.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts without shell

indicators.note: removing the shell leaves only the inside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A snack of fruit and nuts, with the nuts already shelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' seems to be food alongside the fruit, but it means crazy, and BANANAS loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anana is an old name for the pineapple, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Special mince inclined to be cut for lamb kebab

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed, so its last letter is lopped off

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
hash is chopped or minced meat
like can mean likely or inclined to, as in 'like to fail'

explanation.surface: A cook prepares special minced meat for a lamb kebab.
explanation.definitionFit: Shashlik is a Caucasian dish of lamb pieces grilled on a skewer, a kind of kebab.

clue.text: White border once with no end of geranium

indicators.note: being without something means it is taken out of the word

parts.note: margent is an archaic form of margin

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one taken

parts.note: the last letter of geranium

explanation.surface: A white flowerbed edging of old, now planted without any geraniums.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGENT drops its M, the letter that ends geranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Argent is the heraldic name for silver, shown as white on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Number one chance, with friend right away

indicators.note: things sent away are no longer there, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance
oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The top chance goes to a friend once the right one is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPORTUNITY loses OPPO and RT from its front. 'Number one' looks like praise for the chance but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is the mathematical term for the number one.

clue.text: Cell entrance blocked by fellows endlessly

indicators.note: something blocked by another has that thing stuck in its middle

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: fellows are men; the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Men crowd the doorway of a prison cell, blocking the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg, that fuses with another at fertilisation.

clue.text: The college employs bodies on plant

parts.note: t' is the dialect contraction of the, as in northern English
a hall is a college, or its residence
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: The college puts staff to work at a manufacturing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bodies' looks like the staff being employed and 'plant' like a factory; both are botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A thallus is the undivided body of a simple plant such as a seaweed or liverwort, lacking stem, root and leaf.

clue.text: I have an inclination in speech for her

indicators.note: in speech means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to have an inclination is to lean

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they have a soft spot for a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' reads as a romantic liking, but it is a physical slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's name, so it can stand for any 'her'.

clue.text: Obscure hotel around ravine

indicators.note: a thing around another encloses it, so the second word sits inside the first

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
a khor is a dry watercourse or ravine in North Africa

explanation.surface: A remote hotel overlooking a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like a description of the hotel, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkhorn, as in 'inkhorn terms', describes pedantic, learned language that is obscure to ordinary readers.

clue.text: Elegant young girl getting rear pinched

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its end, and pinching it takes it away

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman has her bottom pinched.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable.

clue.text: Purchase in clubs more than once records and Smarties (11, two words)

definitions.note: plural; clever clogs is used for one or many

parts.note: C is clubs in card notation; it opens the answer and appears again later
purchase is mechanical grip or leverage, which a lever gives
the second C for clubs
logs are written records

explanation.surface: Buying sweets at clubs again and again, along with records.
explanation.walkthrough: The purchase goes in among two Cs: C-LEVER-C, then LOGS. Smarties are British chocolate sweets, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever clogs is a know-all, informally a smarty or smart alec.

clue.text: Mostly mentioned clips sounded clearly something like a fiddle

indicators.note: to clip something is to hold it tight within a grip
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: said means mentioned; the last letter is dropped
a bell rang, sounding clearly

explanation.surface: Most of what was said about the clips rang out like a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: SAI, the shortened word, grips RANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarangi is a bowed string instrument of north India, played much as a fiddle is.

clue.text: What I give when fully committed and wild in Perth

definitions.text: What I give when fully committed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving '...' is total commitment
second meaning: an Australian word for wild or untamed

explanation.walkthrough: Perth stands for Australia, where the word is native, from an Aboriginal language.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is total effort; as one, Australian usage for a wild or uncivilised person or animal.

clue.text: Imitation marble so glacial in new design

indicators.note: a new design is a fresh arrangement, so these letters are set out differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fake marble looking so icy in a new scheme of decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Scagliola is plasterwork of gypsum and glue coloured and polished to look like marble.

clue.text: Safe shelter in "new" Durham town

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A secure refuge in a recently built town in County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterlee is one of Britain's post-war new towns, in County Durham, north-east England, hence the quoted 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peterlee was founded in 1948 as a planned new town in County Durham.

clue.text: Bit of embarrassment after dancing act reveals derrière

indicators.note: coming after places this piece behind the other one

parts.note: nach, or nautch, is an Indian dance performance

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its first

parts.note: the opening letter of embarrassment

explanation.surface: A dancer's routine goes embarrassingly wrong and shows their bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' looks like an anagram signal for act, but the dance itself is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Nache is an old word for the rump or buttock, which derrière means.

clue.text: Component of dye as before reduced well in Italy

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: still means as before, continuing
bene is Italian for well

explanation.surface: An ingredient of a dye, still made in Italy as it used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilbene is a hydrocarbon whose derivatives are used in making dyes and optical brighteners.

clue.text: No good, must get late lunch order (11, three words)

indicators.note: must is grape juice in ferment, and fermenting letters are churned into a new order
with no good, the letter standing for good is taken away

parts.note: taken as written; the G for good goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner complains that a late lunch order is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: ET (get without G) and LATE LUNCH are rearranged. 'order' looks like the meal being requested, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To call the tune is to be in control and give the orders, from the idiom 'he who pays the piper calls the tune'.

clue.text: Legendary Golgotha is piece of interment ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a piece of a word is one letter, here its first

parts.note: the first letter of interment

explanation.surface: The legendary Golgotha is a patch of burial ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legendary' reads as an adjective, but here it is a noun, a writer of legends. Golgotha is the place of the Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary is a compiler of saints' legends, and a hagiologist writes the lives of saints.

clue.text: Star in key broadcast

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A celebrity appearing in a major broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' and 'key' suggest a leading performer in an important show.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Duke, otherwise heading for "Shakespeare in Love"

parts.note: or means otherwise

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Shakespeare
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A duke heading off to see the film Shakespeare in Love.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title tempts the solver to treat it as a single unit, but it is split across three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Best in a mess maybe thoroughly upset

parts.note: out means thoroughly or completely, as in 'tired out'
eat can mean worry or trouble, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Someone defeated in a messy situation is completely distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is a military dining hall, so besting someone there means out-eating them.
explanation.definitionFit: To outeat someone is to eat more than them, beating them at a meal such as one in the mess.

clue.text: Rolls is to be entered for nothing in outside film areas

indicators.note: entered for means put in place of, so one piece swaps into another's spot

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O
lots are the outdoor areas of a film studio

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce is to be entered in place of nothing at outdoor film locations.
explanation.walkthrough: IS replaces the O in LOTS. 'Rolls' looks like the car, but it means registers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls in the sense of official registers of names are lists.

clue.text: Concerned with intestines, one former physician years ago leaving hospital

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: leach is an obsolete spelling of leech, the old word for a doctor
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A one-time doctor long retired from the hospital, who specialised in the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Leech once meant physician, from the practice of bloodletting; the old spelling leach loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac means relating to the ileum, the last part of the small intestine.

clue.text: Like a chat perhaps with Gill, not the first

indicators.note: without the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a gill, or ghyll, is a ravine in northern England

explanation.surface: A friendly natter with someone named Gill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chat' looks like a conversation and Gill like a woman's name; a chat is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Avine means birdlike, and the chat is a small songbird.

clue.text: Bible book's used for Vic in malignancy and idleness

indicators.note: something used for another is put in its place

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible
taken as written
viciosity is an old word for viciousness or malignancy

explanation.surface: A scriptural text is drawn on for Vic during a cancer illness and a period of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: OT replaces VIC at the start of VICIOSITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiosity is the state of being otiose, meaning idle or at leisure.

clue.text: One left old-timer returning for money as before

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left
an OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: A pensioner abandoned and coming back for his old money.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP stands for old-age pensioner, a British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Paoli is the plural of paolo, an old silver coin of the Papal States, so it is currency of former times.

clue.text: Groundsel, perhaps wild seen on Channel Islands round

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Wild groundsel spotted growing on the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British Crown dependencies off Normandy, such as Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is one species of the large plant genus Senecio, which also includes ragwort.

clue.text: Lied about old age

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told a fib about their advanced years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lied' could also be a German song, but here it is just the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eild is a Scots and archaic word for age, especially old age.

clue.text: Striking content of red wine (German)

parts.note: tannin is a substance found in red wine
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A red German wine with a remarkable taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like praise for the wine, but it is a beating; 'content of' suggests a hidden word but simply describes what the wine contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanning is a thrashing, so it is the act of striking someone repeatedly.

clue.text: Muse on second article by Head, mostly for a Greek scholar

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry
S is the abbreviation for second
the definite article
a ness is a headland; the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A thinker muses on a second piece written by the head teacher, chiefly for a Greek academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder; it is one of the nine Muses. 'on' and 'by' just place the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Eratosthenes was the Greek scholar of Alexandria who estimated the circumference of the Earth.
